seller_questions: Can you send the VIN and a photo of the title showing it is clean and in your name?
Can you send a photo of the instrument cluster with the ignition on, showing the full odometer reading and no warning lights?
How long have you owned the car, and how many owners does the Carfax/AutoCheck show? The 9-series plate suggests recent CA registration: was it brought in from another state or re-plated?
Has the car ever been on a track, at autocross, or at a drift event, and does it use any oil between changes?
Has the ECU ever been flashed (OFT, EcuTek or similar), even if it was later returned to stock?
Do you have dated receipts for brake fluid, coolant, transmission and differential fluid, and oil changes? What are the papers on the back seat?
Is the clutch original, and is there any slip in 4th–6th or a chirp from the throwout bearing at idle with the pedal released?
What are the DOT date codes and brand on all four tires?
Has the car had any paintwork, bodywork or windshield replacement?
Will you provide a fresh California smog certificate at sale?
Can a mobile inspector do a pre-purchase inspection at your home in Atwater, including an OBD scan, before any deposit?
Can you send a cold-start video from fully cold, plus photos of the underside and the lower edge of the front bumper?
ppi_focus: OBD scan: ECU calibration ID versus the factory calibration, readiness monitors, stored/pending codes, and any misfire counters or over-rev history.
Clutch engagement point, slip test in high gear, throwout bearing noise, and smooth shifting into 2nd/3rd when cold (synchro wear signals hard use).
Track-use evidence: tire wear pattern, pad and rotor condition, brake fluid colour, roll-over signs on the front tire shoulders, and tow-hook wear.
Oil level and condition plus a dipstick-to-mileage consumption check. Compression/leakdown if any track history surfaces.
Paint-meter sweep of all panels and a check of the front lower bumper/lip and radiator support for impact or scrape damage.
Underside: subframes, lower control arms, exhaust hangers and oil pan for scrapes; diff and transmission seals for leaks.
Engine bay: stock intake and headers versus aftermarket, a CARB-legal visual for smog, cam-plate/timing-cover seepage, and coolant condition.
Tire DOT date codes, alignment and steering-rack boot condition.
Door, hatch and windshield seals and the trunk floor for water ingress (year-round rain use).
VIN check for open recalls at a Toyota dealer.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: VIN plus a clean history report showing one or two owners, no accidents, and a consistent mileage trail.
Up: dated service records (brake fluid, coolant, gear oils) and a clean mobile PPI confirming a stock ECU, a healthy clutch and a dry underside.
Down: any evidence of track/drift use, a current or removed ECU flash, an accident report, or more than two owners.
Down: a refusal to share the VIN, allow a PPI, or provide a CA smog certificate at sale.
evidence.mission_note: It satisfies the manual, budget and rain-capable requirements and is a simple, inexpensive drivetrain to own and resell. However, Jason has said the BRZ/86 stays out of this search, so at most it works only as a pragmatic enthusiast bridge, not one of the target cars.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes only a black 2017 86 with a 6-speed manual, confirmed in the interior photo, a claimed clean title, and a masked 57,XXX-mile reading. The photos show stock-appearing wheels, exhaust, wing and ride height, glossy straight paint, light driver-seat wear and tinted glass; nothing mechanically wrong is observed. There is no VIN, no history report and no service record, so owner count, accident history, the mileage trail and age-based fluid service are all unknown. The CA 9-series plate hints at recent California registration, which makes the owner and registration history a real question rather than a formality (inference). Both conditional model-critical items, track use and tune status, are open: the stock claim is seller prose, though the visible hardware is consistent with it. The fuel-pump recall item does not apply to a 2017 under the profile's scope. Price sits at the fair-value midpoint, with no established known-work items.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, a lit-cluster photo showing full mileage and no warning lights, and tire date codes, and ask whether a mobile inspector can do a PPI with an OBD calibration scan in Atwater before any deposit.
